---
title: "PEVmean (ridge, PCs)"
description: "The prediction error variance (PEV) measures how uncertain the model predictions are for the test set."
---

The prediction error variance (PEV) measures how uncertain the model predictions are for the test set. TSDFGS sums it over the test individuals.

| | |
|---|---|
| Type | Model-based |
| Direction | Smaller is better |
| Uses a test set | yes |
| Score a given set | `pev_score()` |
| Search with it | `optTrain(method = "PEV")` |

## Definition

With an intercept column added, $B = (X'X + \lambda I)^{-1}$ and $\lambda = 1/p$:

$$\mathrm{PEV} = \mathrm{tr}(X_0 B X_0').$$

Dividing by $n_0$ gives PEVmean. This is the PC-ridge form of Akdemir et al. (2015). The relationship-matrix PEV of Rincent et al. (2012) uses contrasts instead; see [CDmean](criterion-cdmean.html).

## Use in TSDFGS

```{r, eval = TRUE}
library(TSDFGS)
data(geno)
pev_score(geno[1:50, ], geno[51:100, ])
```

```{r, eval = TRUE}
fit <- optTrain(geno, cand = 1:404, n.train = 50, method = "PEV",
                 min.iter = 300, console = FALSE, seed = 1)
fit$OPTtrain

# targeted: the test set is known
fit2 <- optTrain(geno, cand = 1:300, n.train = 50, test = 301:404,
                  method = "PEV", min.iter = 300, console = FALSE, seed = 1)
fit2$OPTtrain
```

The search is a random-start exchange (hill-climbing) search; see [How the scores are computed](methods.html). Use `min.iter` larger than 300 on real data and check `fit$converged`.

## Original work

Akdemir, D., Sanchez, J. I., & Jannink, J.-L. (2015). Optimization of genomic selection training populations with a genetic algorithm. *Genetics Selection Evolution, 47*, 38. <https://doi.org/10.1186/s12711-015-0116-6>

Rincent, R., Laloë, D., Nicolas, S., Altmann, T., Brunel, D., Revilla, P., et al. (2012). Maximizing the reliability of genomic selection by optimizing the calibration set of reference individuals: comparison of methods in two diverse groups of maize inbreds (*Zea mays* L.). *Genetics, 192*, 715-728. <https://doi.org/10.1534/genetics.112.141473>

**Repository or website of the original authors:** R package STPGA by Akdemir and colleagues: [CRAN.R-project.org/package=STPGA](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=STPGA) (GPL-3). Rincent et al. (2012) give no software link.

## License review

Formulas and algorithms are ideas and methods, which copyright does not protect. Where an original package is under a GPL license, we read it to check our results and credit it; TSDFGS is [GPL-3](https://github.com/oumarkme/TSDFGS/blob/main/LICENSE.md), which is compatible with GPL-3 and GPL (>= 3) code. This is our reading of the public record, not legal advice; see the [license review](criteria-license-review.html).

* **Original software:** STPGA, GPL-3; we compared outputs and did not copy code.
* **Article license:** Akdemir et al. (2015) CC BY 4.0; Rincent et al. (2012) CHORUS public access.
* **Patents:** none in the articles. TrainSel (2021) says its concepts may be patented; PEV predates it and TSDFGS does not use TrainSel.
* **Verdict:** included.
